# Flow: `jl-flow`

Nodes joined by edges, to move, connect and extend: a workflow editor.

- Class `JlFlow`, a organism: `import { JlFlow } from '@syware/jlib';`
- On the site: https://bioleyl.github.io/jlib/components/flow

A flow of nodes joined by edges, to edit: the steps of a workflow, the stages of a pipeline, the
screens of a journey. People drag nodes (they snap to an 8-pixel grid), draw an edge from an exit to another node,
select an edge and remove it with its button or Delete. They move the view by dragging the background or with two
fingers, and zoom with Ctrl or ⌘ and the wheel, a pinch, or the buttons. With the focus on a node (Tab), the arrows
move it, Shift for further, and Delete removes it; Escape clears the selection. The wand lays the nodes out again:
each a row below the nodes leading to it, under the exit it hangs from (layout() does the same from code).

The graph is plain data. A node has an id, a label and a position (its top left corner), and optionally a
description, a detail (a third line, under a dashed rule; the node is then taller), an icon, a tone (the icon's
colour) or a color of the page's own, start (nothing leads to it) and ports: its exits, left to right along its
bottom edge, each with an id, a label and a tone (the colour of its edges). Without ports a node has one exit; with an
empty list, none. An edge has an id, from, to, and the port it leaves by (the first one when absent).

A node can also show how a run went: its status (running, done, waiting or failed) and taken, the exit it left by;
that exit and its edges to nodes that ran stand out. problem marks what to fix before the flow can run.

Every edit goes out as a whole new graph in change: keep it, save it. The flow does not invent nodes: + on a free
exit, or an edge dropped on empty space, emits add with where the node should go, and the page adds the node and its
edge to the graph (a menu of node kinds, a dialog, or a plain step, as in the examples). With drop-type, things
dragged from the page (a palette of node kinds) are taken too: drop says what was dropped, and where.

## Use

```ts
import { JlFlow } from '@syware/jlib';
```

```tsx
<JlFlow
  graph={{"edges":[{"id":"e1","from":"placed","to":"pack"}],"nodes":[{"id":"placed","label":"Order placed","position":{"x":0,"y":0},"description":"Shop","icon":"inbox","start":true},{"id":"pack","label":"Pack it","position":{"x":0,"y":136},"description":"Warehouse","icon":"package","ports":[{"id":"ready","label":"Ready"},{"id":"missing","label":"Missing","tone":"danger"}]}]}}
  label="Order"
/>
```

```html
<jl-flow
  graph='{"edges":[{"id":"e1","from":"placed","to":"pack"}],"nodes":[{"id":"placed","label":"Order placed","position":{"x":0,"y":0},"description":"Shop","icon":"inbox","start":true},{"id":"pack","label":"Pack it","position":{"x":0,"y":136},"description":"Warehouse","icon":"package","ports":[{"id":"ready","label":"Ready"},{"id":"missing","label":"Missing","tone":"danger"}]}]}'
  label="Order"
></jl-flow>
```

## Properties

Inputs: a JSX prop sets one, code calls `.set(value)` and `.get()`, HTML writes the attribute (lists and objects as JSON).

- `graph` (attribute `graph`): `FlowGraph`, default `{ nodes: [], edges: [] }`. The nodes (id, label, position, and optionally description, detail, icon, tone, color, ports, start, status, taken, problem) and the edges (id, from, port, to).
- `selected` (attribute `selected`): `string`, default `''`. The id of the selected node; the view moves to show it.
- `readonly` (attribute `readonly`): `boolean`, default `false`. View only: nodes can be selected, not moved, joined or removed.
- `dropType` (attribute `drop-type`): `string`, default `''`. The drag-and-drop type the canvas takes (application/x-step): something dragged in carrying it is dropped with drop.
- `label` (attribute `label`): `string`, default `''`. The canvas’s name for screen readers: “Flow” when empty.

## Events

In JSX, the `on…` prop, its handler given the detail; in code, `events.register(name, (detail) => …)`. They do not bubble.

- `change` (`onChange` in JSX), detail `FlowGraph`: The graph after an edit: a node moved, joined, removed.
- `select` (`onSelect` in JSX), detail `string`: A node was selected: its id, or an empty string for none.
- `add` (`onAdd` in JSX), detail `{ from: string; port: string; position: FlowPoint }`: Asks for a node after an exit: the node and exit to join it to, and where to put it.
- `drop` (`onDrop` in JSX), detail `{ data: string; position: FlowPoint }`: Something carrying drop-type was dropped on the canvas: what it carried, and where a node centred on the drop goes.

## Slots

- `empty`: Shown in the middle of the canvas while there is no node.

## Methods

- `fit(): void`: Moves and zooms the view to show every node.
- `reveal(id: string): void`: Moves the view, when needed, so that the node is in sight: one just added, for instance.
- `positionAfter(from: string, port: string): FlowPoint`: Where a node added after an exit goes, as + puts it: a row below, under that exit. For a node the page adds from a menu of its own.
- `centerPosition(): FlowPoint`: Where a node added without a place goes: centred in the view (its top left corner).
- `layout(): void`: Lays the nodes out again, as the wand does: in rows from the starts down, each under the exit it hangs from. Emits change, then shows every node.

## Styling

- `base` (part, `::part(base)`): The canvas.
- `node` (part, `::part(node)`): A node; also named start or selected when it is one.
- `icon` (part, `::part(icon)`): The square around a node’s icon.
- `label` (part, `::part(label)`): A node’s label.
- `description` (part, `::part(description)`): A node’s description.
- `detail` (part, `::part(detail)`): A node’s detail line, under its dashed rule.
- `status` (part, `::part(status)`): The round mark of a node’s status in a run.
- `problem` (part, `::part(problem)`): The mark of a node with something to fix.
- `port` (part, `::part(port)`): An exit: its dot, its label and its + button.
- `edge` (part, `::part(edge)`): An edge’s line; also named selected, or taken when a run went that way.

## Examples

HTML as the site renders it, with its layout classes (`row`, `stack`, `narrow`, `muted`), which are not jlib's: a view writes the same components by class in JSX. A script's `root` is the example's element.

### A workflow

Drag the nodes, draw an edge from an exit to a node, press + under Pay it back to add a step after it, then the wand to tidy up.

```html
<jl-flow class="expenses" label="Expense claim" style="height: 520px"></jl-flow>
```

```js
const expenses = {
  edges: [
    { id: 'e1', from: 'sent', to: 'check' },
    { id: 'e2', from: 'check', port: 'yes', to: 'approve' },
    { id: 'e3', from: 'check', port: 'no', to: 'pay' },
    { id: 'e4', from: 'approve', port: 'refused', to: 'tell' },
    { id: 'e5', from: 'approve', port: 'approved', to: 'pay' },
  ],
  nodes: [
    {
      id: 'sent',
      label: 'Expense sent',
      position: { x: 0, y: 0 },
      description: 'Form',
      icon: 'inbox',
      start: true,
    },
    {
      id: 'check',
      label: 'Over 500?',
      position: { x: 0, y: 136 },
      description: 'Condition',
      icon: 'git-branch',
      ports: [{ id: 'yes', label: 'Yes' }, { id: 'no', label: 'No' }],
      tone: 'warn',
    },
    {
      id: 'approve',
      label: 'Ask the manager',
      position: { x: -160, y: 272 },
      description: 'Approval',
      icon: 'user',
      ports: [
        { id: 'refused', label: 'Refused', tone: 'danger' },
        { id: 'approved', label: 'Approved', tone: 'ok' },
      ],
      tone: 'info',
    },
    {
      id: 'tell',
      label: 'Tell the employee',
      position: { x: -320, y: 408 },
      description: 'Email',
      icon: 'mail',
      ports: [],
    },
    {
      id: 'pay',
      label: 'Pay it back',
      position: { x: 160, y: 408 },
      description: 'Payment',
      icon: 'credit-card',
      tone: 'ok',
    },
  ],
};

const flow = root.querySelector('jl-flow.expenses');
flow.graph.set(expenses);

// + on a free exit, or an edge dropped on empty space: the page adds the node, and its edge.
flow.events.register('add', ({ from, port, position }) => {
  const { edges, nodes } = flow.graph.get();
  const id = `step-${nodes.length + 1}`;
  flow.graph.set({
    edges: [...edges, { id: `edge-${id}`, from, port, to: id }],
    nodes: [...nodes, { id, label: `Step ${nodes.length + 1}`, icon: 'zap', position }],
  });
  flow.selected.set(id);
});
```

### Several exits

ports lists a node's exits, left to right. A tone colours an exit and its edges; danger ones are
dashed. Each edge names the exit it leaves by in port. Wait a day loops back up to the check: its edge goes around.
Connect or remove an edge, and watch the list.

```html
<div class="stack">
  <jl-flow class="payment" label="Payment" style="height: 480px"></jl-flow>
  <jl-code-block class="edge-list" language="ts" heading="graph.edges"></jl-code-block>
</div>
```

```js
const payment = {
  edges: [
    { id: 'e1', from: 'order', to: 'check' },
    { id: 'e2', from: 'check', port: 'paid', to: 'ship' },
    { id: 'e3', from: 'check', port: 'failed', to: 'cancel' },
    { id: 'e4', from: 'check', port: 'pending', to: 'wait' },
    { id: 'e5', from: 'wait', to: 'check' },
  ],
  nodes: [
    { id: 'order', label: 'Order placed', position: { x: 0, y: 0 }, icon: 'inbox', start: true },
    {
      id: 'check',
      label: 'Check the payment',
      position: { x: 0, y: 136 },
      icon: 'credit-card',
      ports: [
        { id: 'paid', label: 'Paid', tone: 'ok' },
        { id: 'failed', label: 'Failed', tone: 'danger' },
        { id: 'pending', label: 'Pending', tone: 'warn' },
      ],
    },
    {
      id: 'ship',
      label: 'Ship the order',
      position: { x: -272, y: 272 },
      icon: 'package',
      ports: [],
      tone: 'ok',
    },
    {
      id: 'cancel',
      label: 'Cancel the order',
      position: { x: 0, y: 272 },
      icon: 'circle-x',
      ports: [],
      tone: 'danger',
    },
    { id: 'wait', label: 'Wait a day', position: { x: 272, y: 272 }, icon: 'clock', tone: 'warn' },
  ],
};

const flow = root.querySelector('jl-flow.payment');
const list = root.querySelector('.edge-list');
const showEdges = (graph) => list.code.set(graph.edges.map((edge) => JSON.stringify(edge)).join('\n'));
flow.graph.set(payment);
showEdges(payment);
flow.events.register('change', showEdges);
```

### What a node shows

Every node has an id, a label and a position; the rest is optional. An icon is any registered
name, and a tone is one of neutral, accent (the default), ok, warn, danger and info.

```html
<jl-flow class="options" label="Node options" readonly style="height: 300px"></jl-flow>
```

```js
const options = {

    {
      id: 'described',

    {

      position: { x: 0, y: 136 },

      icon: 'circle-check',
      tone: 'ok',
    },
    {
      id: 'start',
      label: 'A start',
      position: { x: 272, y: 136 },
      description: 'start: true, no input',
      icon: 'zap',
      start: true,
    },
    {

};

root.querySelector('jl-flow.options').graph.set(options);
```

### A run, and what to fix

A test run, drawn on the flow: status on each node that ran, taken on the exits they left by
(those exits, and the edges to nodes that ran, stand out), and problem on a node with something to fix. detail adds a
third line; color gives an icon a colour of the page's own.

```html
<jl-flow class="run" label="Invoice approval" readonly style="height: 560px"></jl-flow>
```


### Dropped from a palette

drop-type names what the canvas takes from the page: drag a step from the row onto the flow, and the page adds it where it lands.

```html
<div class="stack">
  <div class="row">
    <jl-chip label="Send an email" icon="mail" draggable="true" data-step="Send an email"></jl-chip>
    <jl-chip label="Wait a day" icon="clock" draggable="true" data-step="Wait a day"></jl-chip>
  </div>
  <jl-flow class="dropped" label="Steps" drop-type="application/x-demo-step" style="height: 320px"></jl-flow>
</div>
```

```js
const start = {
  edges: [],
  nodes: [{ id: 'start', label: 'Start', position: { x: 0, y: 0 }, icon: 'zap', start: true }],
};

const flow = root.querySelector('jl-flow.dropped');
flow.graph.set(start);
for (const chip of root.querySelectorAll('[data-step]')) {
  chip.addEventListener('dragstart', (event) =>
    event.dataTransfer.setData('application/x-demo-step', chip.dataset.step)
  );
}
// Dropped on the canvas: the page adds the step where it landed.
flow.events.register('drop', ({ data, position }) => {
  const { edges, nodes } = flow.graph.get();
  const id = `step-${nodes.length + 1}`;
  flow.graph.set({ edges, nodes: [...nodes, { id, label: data, icon: 'zap', position }] });
  flow.selected.set(id);
});
```

### Your own look

The parts restyle the nodes from the page with ::part(): node (also start and selected), icon,
label, description, detail, status, problem, port, edge (also selected and taken), and base, the canvas. Every look
keeps to the design tokens. The sizes stay: the flow computes every edge from the node's box, 240 by 64 pixels (96
with a detail line).

```html
<style>
  jl-flow.styled::part(base) {
    background-color: var(--jl-surface);
    background-image: none;
  }
  jl-flow.styled::part(node) {
    border-radius: var(--jl-radius-pill);
    box-shadow: none;
  }
  jl-flow.styled::part(node start) {
    border-color: var(--jl-accent-line);
    background: var(--jl-accent-soft);
  }
  jl-flow.styled::part(node selected) {
    border-color: var(--jl-text);
  }
  jl-flow.styled::part(icon) {
    border-radius: var(--jl-radius-pill);
  }
  jl-flow.styled::part(port) {
    letter-spacing: 0.04em;
    text-transform: uppercase;
  }
  jl-flow.styled::part(edge) {
    stroke-width: 1.5;
  }
</style>
<jl-flow class="styled" label="Order" style="height: 420px"></jl-flow>
```

### Empty

The empty slot shows while there is no node: say how to start.

```html
<jl-flow class="blank" label="New workflow" style="height: 300px">
  <div slot="empty" class="stack" style="align-items: center">
    <strong>How does it start?</strong>
    <jl-button class="first" icon="plus" label="Add a start"></jl-button>
  </div>
</jl-flow>
```

```js
const start = {
  edges: [],
  nodes: [{ id: 'start', label: 'Start', position: { x: 0, y: 0 }, icon: 'zap', start: true }],
};

const flow = root.querySelector('jl-flow.blank');
root.querySelector('.first').events.register('press', () => flow.graph.set(start));

// + on a free exit, or an edge dropped on empty space: the page adds the node, and its edge.
flow.events.register('add', ({ from, port, position }) => {
  const { edges, nodes } = flow.graph.get();
  const id = `step-${nodes.length + 1}`;
  flow.graph.set({
    edges: [...edges, { id: `edge-${id}`, from, port, to: id }],
    nodes: [...nodes, { id, label: `Step ${nodes.length + 1}`, icon: 'zap', position }],
  });
  flow.selected.set(id);
});
```
